description:
FILED s470bs (Opus) as the measured RESIDUE of #1033, which is otherwise
closed.

REPRO (scratch/s470bs/p01b.pl rows 28-31):

    open(my $cl, '<', '/etc/passwd') or die; close $cl;
    $! = 0; my $e = -e $cl;      printf "errno=%d\n", $!+0;
    $! = 0; my @b = stat($cl);   printf "errno=%d\n", $!+0;

  perl 5.40.3:  9  9   (EBADF â the glob is still in $cl)
  PCL:          2  2   (ENOENT)

CAUSE, located: `%p-forget-fh`'s last box arm is `(box-set fh *p-undef*)` â
closing a LEXICAL handle empties the box.  The stat operand resolver then sees
undef, which is perl's EMPTY PATH (`-e undef` IS ENOENT, probed), so the answer
is right for undef and wrong for a closed handle: PCL cannot tell them apart
because they are the same value.

WHY IT WAS NOT CHANGED HERE: that clearing is DELIBERATE and something else
depends on it.  `%p-fileno-impl`'s contract (task #529) is "undef for a handle
that is not open â never opened, closed, an empty lexical, a closed glob, a
closed name", and `p-defined-fh` reads the same emptiness.  Making a closed
lexical keep something stat-visible is a change to what a closed handle IS in
the box model, not a change to the stat family, and it needs its own probe set
(`defined($fh)`, `fileno($fh)`, `print $fh`, `eof($fh)` after close) plus a
sweep.

NO ROW COST MEASURED: `t/op/stat_errors.t` uses BAREWORD handles
(CLOSEDFILE, CLOSEDDIR, SCALARFILE), and all three answer EBADF correctly
since s470bs.  Guard rows 50/55 of `Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t` cover those;
this shape has no guard row precisely because it is still wrong.
=== DONE (s473f) ===
FIXED.  %p-forget-fh no longer empties the box: perl leaves the glob in $fh, so
`defined $fh` stays 1, `"$fh"` stays GLOB(0x...), `ref($fh)` stays GLOB, and a
stat/filetest on the closed handle is EBADF instead of the ENOENT of the empty
PATH that undef used to become.  #529's `fileno` contract is untouched -- it
reads `open-stream-p`, not emptiness.

WHAT THE TASK ASKED FOR AND THE PROBE ANSWERED: a CLOSED STREAM now reaches
callers that never saw one.  print/printf and the readers are right for FREE
(`output-stream-p` and `input-stream-p` are both NIL for a closed stream --
measured), while tell/seek/sysseek/binmode/getc/read/sysread/syswrite/select
would SIGNAL, so they ask the new %p-live-stream -- ONE spelling of the test,
NOT in `p-get-stream`, which is the hot path of every print and readline
(-6.4 % measured when it was there).

Two divergences the same probe found, in the two functions the change touches:
syswrite on a handle that is not open now sets EBADF, and truncate no longer
falls back to truncating a file NAMED after a closed lexical -- its failure
answer is perl's undef, not '', and an UNDEF designator is perl's empty PATH
(ENOENT), not a handle (EBADF).

It also unblocked what %p-out-fh-or-fail's docstring said was unimplementable
(a die on an undef print designator): that note now points at #1421.
Guard Pl/t/handle-place-01.t rows 87-115.  Commit 42676dff.
subject: A CLOSED LEXICAL handle in a stat/filetest slot answers ENOENT where perl answers EBADF, because `%p-forget-fh` clears the box to undef and the operand is then the empty PATH.  (The bareword, dirhandle and in-memory spellings are all EBADF since s470bs.)
